title: Durable resource and integration recovery inventory providers
description: Objective: supply the missing production recovery-window enumeration sources for scheduler resource effects and integration attempts so the recovery coordinator never infers absence from a generic event scan or a fixture. Deliverable: durable resource and integration attempt inventory records/readers bound to project, effect intent, cursor window and current recovery incarnation, plus immutable RecoveryInventoryRegistration fragments or an equally explicit typed bridge the daemon can compose with @moe/runner registrations. MEASURED GAP at HEAD c0c5929: @moe/scheduler exposes ResourceRow transition functions but no durable inventory enumerator/reader; there is no production integration-attempt record or integration inventory surface in scheduler/store/daemon, and store schema/root probes find no resource/integration inventory rows. The runner collector rejects unknown/extra class evidence. Consumer: task-cf7fb147bd1c47698cbd65c9535370aa. NOT in scope: node-side adapters, adoption/quarantine decisions, project embargo, caller-selected current binding, or recovery.complete. Owned paths: focused scheduler/store contracts and daemon-facing adapters selected after re-measurement; do not grow existing >250-line files. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test && pnpm --filter @moe/store test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck.
definitionOfDone: A production durable reader enumerates every project-tagged scheduler resource effect in an exact backup-cursor window, including QUARANTINED/non-fenceable states, and binds each row to its effect intent and source proof digest; empty is COMPLETE only with a verifiable negative proof.

A production durable integration-attempt record and reader enumerate every project-tagged integration target/effect in the same window with exact intent/incarnation binding; unmatched, malformed, duplicate, truncated, or unreadable records stay UNKNOWN with stable code and originating layer.

The daemon-facing bridge exposes immutable registration fragments for the resource and integration populations without mutable global registration, caller-provided item lists, or reimplementation of scheduler/store authority.

Persistence/reopen tests prove resource and integration rows survive process/store reopen and are filtered by exact project/cursor/incarnation; refusal tests assert exact stable code and layer and generated class/case sweeps assert non-zero cardinality.
Focused mutation drills alter each production completeness/fenceability comparison and turn the named resource or integration test red.
Fresh pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test && pnpm --filter @moe/store test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck exits 0, with repo-wide foreign red disclosed by owned-path baseline.
taskRails: Do not infer durable inventory from caller-supplied fixtures or by scanning generic events without a typed complete-population contract.
Do not convert restored counters or a caller-selected incarnation into recovery authority; bind to the selected store/anchor current binding.
Missing/unreadable/partial enumeration stays UNKNOWN and preserves the precise upstream code/layer.
If shared schema or wire contracts change, run full regression as required by the global schema rail.
Target <=250 physical lines per production source and split before 400; the cap is per file.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the exact durable contract and canonical codec. Define the closed `RESOURCE | INTEGRATION_TARGET` vocabulary, caller basis (project tag plus backup cursor/generation only), internal selected scope (store project plus anchored incarnation/key epoch/binding digest), resource and integration observation unions, window seal, immutable class fragment, and typed registration shapes. Caller inputs must have exact own enumerable data keys and cannot contain current refs, counters, item arrays, or authority fields. Canonical bytes use one field order, bounded sizes/counts, deterministic code-point ordering, a body digest, semantic revalidation before digest acceptance, and byte-for-byte re-encode checks. Reuse the daemon's already-admitted stable upstream tuples: invalid input, missing record/seal, unreadable/noncanonical bytes, duplicate/conflict/count mismatch, truncated coverage, and binding mismatch remain UNKNOWN at `INVENTORY_ADAPTER`; add no new authority or disposition. Keep the TS source <=250 lines and add the exact one-line LF runtime bridge.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the durable provider over the public store surface, with no SQLite/schema access. On every append, seal, and read, derive project identity from `getHealth`, read the ACTIVE recovery binding, read the matching daemon anchor, and require exact incarnation/key epoch/binding/generation agreement; never accept those refs from the caller. Persist one canonical observation per call through deterministic `commitExpectedVersionDecision` identities into a dedicated aggregate addressed by project, backup cursor/generation, and current incarnation. Snapshot `ResourceRow` exhaustively (including state, capacity, epoch, external, and a closed FENCEABLE/NON_FENCEABLE projection) without reimplementing scheduler transitions; bind resource identity as `(resourceId,effectIntentRef)`. Bind integration identity as `(attemptRef,targetRef,effectIntentRef)` plus intent digest and source proof. Replay identical writes, refuse divergent duplicates, and serialize append versus seal by expected aggregate version so no post-seal row can succeed.
implementationPlan.note: No production bytes changed in this reopen; durable-recovery-inventory.ts (315 lines) stands as landed at fc35d14, sha256-verified identical after all five drills. QA's reopen did not fault the writer: appends/seals still derive project identity from getHealth, bind the ACTIVE binding and anchor, and serialize by expected version. The reopen work touches the writer only as the surface the new forgery tests must NOT be allowed to bypass silently — each forged payload is committed through the same public `commitExpectedVersionDecision` shape the writer uses, into the aggregate `resolveDurableWindow` names, and the honest-forgery control in each test is accepted, so the tamper is the only variable.

implementationPlan.description: Complete the same provider with the sealed reader and daemon composition seam. Read only the dedicated aggregate with bounded pagination, require exact sequence/decision trace/event types, canonical bytes, unique identities, one final seal, exact counts/digests, and positions `(backupCursor,endInclusive]`; missing/partial/unreadable evidence returns the precise UNKNOWN tuple and never a partial list. Export a frozen literal two-registration tuple/factory whose enumerators accept only basis/window, recheck the selected binding, return frozen raw observations plus proof fragments, and never decide adoption, quarantine, signing authority, or `recovery.complete`; no mutable global registry or caller item list. implementationPlan.note: Adversarial review of the reopen diff (test file only) found three things and all three were fixed before commit, then the whole gate was re-run. (1) `honestSeal` picked the source proof by ARRAY INDEX, so a reordered class list would have handed the resource population the integration proof and the control would still have passed; now keyed on the class name itself. (2) `resolveFor` carried an unused third parameter — dead surface in a helper whose whole job is to be trusted; removed. (3) The honest-seal control asserted only ok:true, which an empty or partial answer also satisfies; it now pins observations to rows + INTEGRATIONS, so the control cannot pass on a shortened population. Checklist items considered and cleared: every test registers its stores through `open()` and its temp dirs through `newDirectory()`, so the afterEach drain still closes them when `forgeEvent`/`resolveFor` THROW, not only on success — no Windows handle can outlive a failing forgery; tests using two stores register both; no test hand-builds a ResourceRow or reimplements a transition; `pos(99)` is inside (042,100] and collides with no generated position (rows use 043..051, integrations 070..072), and the assertion pins that it actually moved; the sweep asserts BOTH that 9 perturbations were generated and that all 10 digests are distinct, so it cannot pass by generating nothing; `resourceClass.itemCount > 1` is asserted before `slice(1)`, so the tamper is never vacuous; no `.only`/`.skip`/`.todo`. Known coupling, disclosed rather than hidden: `honestSeal` mirrors what the production sealer commits, so if the seal contract moves the fixture goes stale — but it fails LOUD, because the honest-forgery control demands production still accept it. Gate re-run after the review edits: the exact chain `pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test && pnpm --filter @moe/store test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck` fresh in the foreground, GATE_EXIT=0, scheduler 43/1319, store 41/469, daemon 76/1631, typecheck 0 errors. reopenReason:
I re-ran the full gate myself at HEAD fc35d14 and it is green exactly as reported: scheduler 43 files/1319 tests, store 41/469, daemon 76/1625, pnpm typecheck 0 errors, all four legs captured to separate files (SCHED=0 STORE=0 DAEMON=0 TYPECHECK=0). Commit fc35d14 touches only the nine owned paths, the four .js bridges are one-line LF, per-file counts are 257/261/315/355 (all under the 400 hard cap), and the focused file runs 25 tests. I also re-ran three of your drills independently and they are real: hardcoding fenceability to FENCEABLE reddens "projects every ResourceRow onto its exact fenceability" ("expected 'FENCEABLE' to be 'NON_FENCEABLE'"), disabling the PROOF_MISSING guard reddens "calls an empty class COMPLETE only when a negative proof is bound", and `>` to `>=` on the window start reddens "excludes the start cursor and includes the end cursor". DoD 1, 3, 5 and 6 hold.

DoD 2 and DoD 4 do not. Three production guards are drill-dead — I mutated each and the entire 25-test file stayed green:

1. reader.ts:170 — dropped the `storeProjectId !== projectId` clause: 25/25 pass.
2. contract.ts:247 — set projectId and projectTag to "" inside durableInventoryScopeDigest: 25/25 pass.
3. reader.ts:305 — replaced the seal digest comparison AND the sameDurableBytes re-encode check with `if (false) return R.UNREADABLE;`: 25/25 pass.

So "filtered by exact project" (DoD 4) has zero coverage in either mechanism, and the tamper-detection surface DoD 2 names is unasserted: RECOVERY_INVENTORY_RECORD_UNREADABLE appears 0 times in the test file while the other nine refusal codes all appear. Every test opens with PROJECT_ID and passes PROJECT_ID, so the mismatch branch is never taken.

All my drill edits were reversed with Edit; sha256 and `git status --porcelain apps/daemon/src/recovery/` confirm the tree is back to committed bytes. Fix only these three; the rest of the diff is sound.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Use the task's explicit 'equally explicit typed bridge' option, implemented inside the daemon over the existing public SqliteEventStore decision/event API. Rejected widening @moe/runner: its RecoveryInventoryRegistration class union is intentionally frozen to four node-side classes and cannot represent RESOURCE or INTEGRATION_TARGET. Rejected dedicated SQLite tables/schema v5: it would add migration/schema ownership without improving the required post-restore inventory proof and would exceed this task's focused file budget. Rejected a global readEventsAfter scan or caller item array: neither proves complete population. The selected design uses one dedicated, incarnation-addressed aggregate with typed row events and a terminal two-class seal; reads use readAggregateEvents for that aggregate only. Rejected adding scheduler persistence: ResourceRow already is the scheduler authority, so the daemon snapshots that public type without duplicating its transitions.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Remeasured rather than trusting the stale task snapshot. At planning HEAD 275986add4c5e0a05c3f654eb67e40fed83418bf, `git rev-parse HEAD:apps/daemon/src/recovery/recovery-inventory-contract.ts` returned 6ed4a8a473297d6e502b1c2a9266cf4f9f9cd25c. That committed contract freezes six proofs/seven populations, with RESOURCE->[RESOURCE] and INTEGRATION_TARGET->[INTEGRATION_TARGET]; runner remains four-class only. `rg` found @moe/scheduler's root-exported ResourceRow with resourceId/capacityUnits/epoch/state/effectIntentRef/external/fenceable and PENDING_ACQUIRE|ACTIVE|RELEASED|QUARANTINED production transitions, but no durable resource inventory and no production IntegrationAttempt anywhere in scheduler/store/daemon. SqliteEventStore already exposes commitExpectedVersionDecision, readAggregateEvents, getHealth, and readRecoveryBinding, so no schema/root-store change is needed. `apps/daemon/package.json` declares both @moe/scheduler and @moe/store as workspace dependencies; pnpm-lock.yaml's apps/daemon importer contains both. A temporary compiled probe under apps/daemon/src/recovery imported ResourceRow from bare @moe/scheduler and SqliteEventStore from bare @moe/store, `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` exited 0, and the probe was deleted in the same command. The five planned paths were absent and clean; foreign .moe and apps/daemon/src/activation WIP are explicitly excluded.
planningNotes.risks: The seal must prove exact cardinality/order for both classes; `every()` without a two-class count is vacuous. A seal digest by itself is not completeness unless it binds the typed source proofs, row identities/digests, project, backup cursor/generation, selected anchor/incarnation/key epoch, and exact end cursor. Concurrent append/seal must use expected-version serialization so a row cannot appear after a successful seal. Duplicate identity is (resourceId,effectIntentRef) for resources and (attemptRef,targetRef,effectIntentRef) for integrations, preserving distinct attempts while refusing conflicting repeats. No bridge result may decide ADOPTED/QUARANTINED or grant recovery.complete. Keep both new production TS files <=250 physical lines; exact one-line LF .js bridges are required. File-backed reopen tests must close every SQLite handle before Windows temp-directory cleanup. Consumer composition remains task-cf7fb147bd1c47698cbd65c9535370aa; do not treat that downstream blocked task as a prerequisite.
